mappings.note: Asks for the most and least reactive of four named metals - the 'arranges metals in order of reactivity' half of LO-2, with no displacement prediction needed.
Graphite as the conducting non-metal is the classic exception used when classifying by electrical conductivity - LO-1.
Names the metal that breaks the nitric-acid rule. The contrast is acid behaviour, not metal ranking, so LO-1's chemical-property clause rather than LO-2.

POOR FIT. The answer, PVC, is a polymer and not a non-metallic element at all; the item tests a materials-use fact. LO-1 is the nearest legal code because the underlying idea is that non-metals do not conduct. Recorded as a content defect.
The required explanation is copper's position below hydrogen in the reactivity series - explicitly series reasoning (LO-2), unlike the generic metal+acid property items mapped to LO-1.
Four metal/salt-solution pairs must be screened for feasibility; only ranking Mg, Zn, Fe, Pb and Cu settles it - the predictive use of the series named in LO-2.

Defines electrovalent compounds as formed by electron transfer from metal to non-metal. That is compound formation, which C 1.1 names at competency level but which no learning outcome under it covers.

Electrolytic refining apparatus - the refining stage of LO-6. DEFECT: the four options are bare figure labels (a)-(d) with no figure rendered in the item, so it is unanswerable as stored; mapped on the explanation text.
Electron loss and gain written out for Na and Cl. Ion formation from electronic configuration is competency-level content (Bohr model, valency); no outcome in this chapter's frame covers it.

Matching elements to conductivity, allotropy and uses. The conductivity and allotrope rows are LO-1 property classification; the food-preservative and ammonia rows are uses-recall that no outcome covers, which is why only LO-1 is cited.
Solubility of ionic compounds in water versus organic solvents - a property of compounds, not of elements, so LO-1 does not reach it and the competency is the closest legal code.
WEAK FIT. Four alloys matched to their constituent metals. Composition recall, cited to LO-7 only because alloying appears nowhere else in the outcome layer.

Metallic lustre as a defining physical property - LO-1. The assertion-reason wrapper does not change the content demand.

The answer is stated in series terms ('metals at the bottom of the activity series'), so LO-2 leads; LO-6 is cited second for occurrence. This is the reverse order from the native-state MCQ, where specific metals had to be recalled and occurrence was the demand.
Both assertion and reason are physical properties of metals (sonority, conduction); the item tests whether one explains the other. Wholly within LO-1.
The complement of the free-state item and it honestly shares its codes: top-of-series metals are never found free. Ranking (LO-2) drives the answer, occurrence (LO-6) is the context.
Turns on metal oxides being basic rather than acidic, with amphoterism as the exception - the chemical-property clause of LO-1.

Asks for the low/medium/high reactivity banding itself, which is arranging metals by reactivity (LO-2). LO-6 uses the same three bands but only as the input to extraction, and no extraction is asked for here.
Displacement of copper by sodium, with the reason stating the general displacement rule - LO-2's predictive clause verbatim.
The demand is which ore forms (oxides, sulphides, carbonates) middle-reactivity metals occur as, so LO-6 leads; LO-2 is cited second for the 'middle of the activity series' criterion.
